extracted.intended_audience: Title IX coordinators, institutional administrators, and compliance officers at K-12 LEAs and postsecondary IHEs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for how recipients (LEAs and IHEs) must adopt and implement Title IX grievance procedures, including evidence disclosure, live hearings with cross-examination, standards of proof, appeals, informal resolution, and related operational choices and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of evidence for inspection and review
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide the evidence to the parties for inspection and review in an electronic format or a hard copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations revised §106.45(b)(5)(vi) to state recipients may provide evidence electronically or as a hard copy. The Department removed a prior reference that might have required use of a file‑sharing platform to alleviate confusion; recipients are not required to use a file‑sharing platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ten‑day periods for evidence inspection and report response
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must be given ten days to inspect and review evidence and ten days to respond to the investigative report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each recipient may choose whether those ten days are calendar days or business days; recipients retain discretion. These two ten‑day periods are intended to allow parties adequate time to inspect/review evidence and respond to the investigative report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live hearings with cross‑examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations require live hearings that permit cross‑examination under §106.45(b)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross‑examination must occur at live hearings; advisors conduct cross‑examination. The regulation permits parties to be in separate rooms with technology enabling simultaneous seeing/hearing of the person answering questions. The Department does not require recipients to construct special hearing rooms or expensive closed‑circuit systems and expects many recipients will use existing equipment or free/low‑cost video conferencing tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of advisor for cross‑examination when a party lacks one
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party does not have an advisor at a postsecondary institution hearing, the recipient must provide, without fee or charge, an advisor of the recipient's choice for the limited purpose of conducting cross‑examination on behalf of that party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.45(b)(6)(i) expressly states the recipient‑provided advisor does not need to be an attorney and need not have specialized training. The advisor's essential function is to relay the party's cross‑examination questions so parties never personally question or confront each other during the hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement that party advisors be attorneys or have specialized training
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisors of choice or recipient‑provided advisors may, but are not required to be, attorneys; there are no requirements that advisors have specialized training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: People other than attorneys may conduct cross‑examination. The Department notes not all attorneys regularly conduct cross‑examination (e.g., transactional attorneys) and anticipates many recipients will assign faculty or staff rather than hire attorneys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient responsibility for providing technology to allow separate rooms
rubrics_metrics.description: At the request of either party, the recipient must allow the live hearing, including cross‑examination, to occur with the parties in separate rooms and with technology allowing the decision‑maker and parties to simultaneously see and hear the person answering questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations do not require recipients to purchase expensive equipment; common solutions (webcams, laptops, cell phones, free conferencing platforms) and simple audio recorders can satisfy the requirement. The Department included an estimated cost of $100 per hearing for audiovisual requirements but believes many recipients can meet requirements at low or no cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording or transcript of hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for audio or audiovisual recordings or a transcript of hearings must be met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department observes these can be accomplished at very low or no cost using voice memo apps, tape recorders, or common software; costs were nonetheless included in the RIA assumptions to ensure coverage where they occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of standard of evidence for determinations regarding responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients have a clear choice to apply either the preponderance of the evidence standard or the clear and convincing evidence standard when reaching determinations regarding responsibility under §106.45(b)(7)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department removed a prior limitation that tied use of preponderance to consistency with non‑sexual misconduct standards. Recipients should consider the effects (protests, litigation risk, campus response) when selecting the standard; the Department will not predict how many will choose either standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of investigator and decision‑maker (no single‑investigator model)
rubrics_metrics.description: The investigator may not be the same person as the decision‑maker under §106.45(b)(7)(i); the single‑investigator model is prohibited for determinations regarding responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Title IX Coordinator may serve as the investigator, provided there is no conflict of interest or bias under §106.45(b)(1)(iii), but cannot serve as the decision‑maker. Recipients may use employee adjudicators or contract with independent/professional decision‑makers; the Department's cost estimates assume hearings will be conducted with independent decision‑makers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals procedures and separate appeals decision‑maker
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer appeals equally to both parties on three specified bases and ensure the appeals decision‑maker is not the same person who served as the Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or original decision‑maker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.45(b)(8) requires appeals rights; the Department declined requests to allow the original decision‑maker to handle appeals. The Department updated burden estimates to include a separate decision‑maker for appeals and notes training assumptions were revised accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal resolution: optional and limited
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are not required to provide an informal resolution process and are expressly prohibited from using informal resolution to resolve allegations that an employee sexually harassed a student under §106.45(b)(9)(iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department adjusted its assumption about the percent of formal complaints resolved through informal resolution to 25 percent overall (up from 10 percent), but noted the 34 percent figure reported in one study applied only to postsecondary institutions and is not broadly reliable because informal resolution is precluded for some complaint types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time commitment estimates for advisors
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department increased estimated advisor time commitments to eight hours per hearing at the LEA level and 60 hours per hearing at the IHE level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change reflects the Department's recognition that advisors may need substantial time with parties outside the hearing itself. These estimates were used in the Regulatory Impact Analysis cost modeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to build dedicated hearing spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations do not mandate recipients construct or renovate dedicated hearing rooms or equip them with expensive AV systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients can reasonably identify suitable existing spaces (offices, classrooms, conference rooms) and use existing equipment paired with software solutions rather than invest in costly new equipment for infrequent hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance procedure and other regulatory amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department amends regulations regarding designation of a Title IX Coordinator, dissemination of nondiscrimination notice, and adoption of grievance procedures to address sex discrimination and sexual harassment, including how to report or file complaints and how the recipient will respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations clarify what conduct constitutes sexual harassment under Title IX and prescribe when and how a recipient must respond to allegations to protect civil rights consistently with constitutional protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that recipients' responses respect constitutional protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX does not require recipients to infringe upon existing constitutional protections; final regulations are intended to be consistent with constitutional due process for misconduct proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department states its final regulations establish expectations in a manner consistent with constitutional rights and may reduce undue litigation risk; recipients should design grievance processes mindful of constitutional protections.
